title: The Carrier Bag Theory of Fiction
creator: Ursula K. Le Guin
why_it_matters: It protects against building only spear-shaped tools. The essay keeps asking what kinds of containers, holdfasts, and carrying structures let more fragile or plural things remain intact.
why_now: The foundry is increasingly about holding continuity, residue, recurrence, and relation. This essay gives language for containers that gather without becoming conquest machines.
active_questions: What is the carrier-bag equivalent of a CLI tool?
How do we build containers for pressure rather than weapons for throughput?
signals: A system can be defined by what it holds, not only by what it drives forward.
Helpful counter-pressure against turning every tool into an efficiency instrument.
notes: Pairs nicely with A Pattern Language when thinking about humane local structure.
Relevant whenever the machine room starts glorifying output velocity.
